title: Christ Church Cathedral, Grafton
geometryBasis: The photographed historic complex and the named extant cathedral are tied by the standing wall outline, east and west faces, and the matching Wikidata identity.
sectionBasis: The published 1888 bird’s-eye view shows the first phase, main roof and lower aisle. Heritage NSW and the cathedral conservators record the 1937 continuation with eight nave bays, west double arch, baptistry, and repeating salmon brick.
limitations: The model represents the single cathedral with attached rooms. Separate cottages, diocesan offices and unbuilt designs are outside the scope.
Individual shaped bricks, glazing patterns and secondary roof measurements are approximate.
